_about: The passages Scripture Memory offers as a weekly suggestion. Canonical locations and editorial metadata only — never a word of Scripture. The words are read out of data/bible/ in whichever edition the reader locked when they began, exactly as every other surface in this app resolves a reference.

_authoring.whatBelongsHere: A passage somebody could reasonably carry in memory: short, coherent on its own, and worth the weeks it will take. Breadth across the canon matters more than covering a topic.
_authoring.whatDoesNot: A verse that only means what people think it means when it is lifted out of its paragraph. Length is not the only test — a short verse can still be a misquotation when it stands alone.
_authoring.status: Every entry is `proposed` until a person has read it in context and approved it. `npm run memory:verify` prints what is still waiting. See MEMORY-REVIEW.md.
deliberatelyExcluded: Jeremiah 29:11 — addressed to exiles in Babylon about a seventy-year timeline, and the single most reliably proof-texted verse in English-speaking Christianity. Memorised alone it teaches the opposite of what it says.
Philippians 4:13 — in context it is about contentment in plenty and in want. Alone it reads as a promise about performance, which is not what Paul wrote.
Proverbs 22:6 — a proverb, which is a genre of general truth rather than a guarantee, and it is routinely carried as a guarantee by parents who then blame themselves.
